boot.mcu_mode: C167-family bootstrap loader (BSL) on ASC0 (RxD0 = P3.11, TxD0 = P3.10), 8N1: after reset the host sends one zero byte, the BSL takes its baud rate from it and answers with an identification byte (C5h = C167 derivatives, D5h = devices with identification registers), then loads exactly 32 bytes of loader code. On EDC15 boards ASC0 reaches the K-line through the board's transceiver.
boot.notes: Board level only: the case has to be opened. No public source documents this route for the EDC15C6 itself: the C167 bootstrap loader is the EDC15 platform's, and grounding flash pin 24 at power-up is reported for the sibling VAG EDC15P in a retailer blog post. Check the CPU marking (C167 family) and the flash chip on your board first. OpenTune's BSL read only reads; it never writes or erases.

points.name: Flash DQ4 to CPU P0L.4/AD4
points.note: Only valid if the board routes flash DQ4 to CPU AD4 (C167CR P-MQFP-144 pin 104 = P0L.4/AD4): confirm continuity between flash pin 24 and CPU pin 104 before using it. The C167CR manual's example pull-down on P0L.4 is 8 kOhm.

boot.reset_timing: P0L.4 must read low at the end of the hardware reset: apply the pull-down before power-up and release it once the BSL has answered (the cited EDC15P post releases after about 5 s; OpenTune's notes cite 2-3 s). P0L.5, P0L.3 and P0L.2 must read high (Table 19-2: P0L.5..2 = 1 0 1 1 selects the standard bootstrap loader). A hardware reset pulse must last at least 1032 TCL (errata CPU.7).

temic-dq250-vag.name: VAG DQ250 / 02E DSG mechatronic (J743, PQ platforms)
temic-dq250-vag.notes: Six-speed wet-clutch DSG (02E) with the mechatronic/TCU (J743) inside the gearbox. Two software generations were seen in real reads: PowerPC (big-endian; ecudef temic-dq250-02e, checksum dq250-02e = CRC-16/MCRF4XX sector table, real-image-tested on six reads) and a later Infineon TriCore build (02E300013N; ecudef temic-dq250-02e-tricore, checksum not located). The DQ250-MQB JAMCRC (checksum id dq250) does NOT apply to 02E. The 02E927770xx numbers are mechatronic (hardware) part numbers; 02E300xxx numbers are the software/gearbox part numbers found in the flash image. Vehicle list and 02E927770 part numbers from MaxxECU's DQ250 integration notes (not exhaustive). Protocols left empty: not stated by the sources.

read_methods.notes: Bench over CAN on the 20-pin T20e plug (ecupinouts lists a K-line variant on pin 1; MaxxECU marks pin 1 K-line as unused). The PowerPC-generation software is handled as a 0x68000-byte (416 KiB) image (12 code sectors + one 32 KiB CAL sector); the TriCore-generation 02E300013N reads seen are 0xB0000 bytes with a 64 KiB CAL first. Reading the CAL over OBD and the OBD programming protocol are not documented in the cited sources; flash containers for 02E are VAG FRF/ODX files (method 0x11 table cipher + compression per vag-tcu-tools), not decoded by OpenTune for 02E yet.

temic-dq250-vag.safety_note: Bench safety: use a current-limited bench supply (12-13.8 V, start with a low current limit) and a fuse in the +12 V lead; connect ground first. Confirm every pin with a multimeter on YOUR unit before applying power - ground pins should show continuity to each other (and usually the housing), and hardware revisions can differ from the sources. A CAN bus needs about 60 ohm between CAN-H and CAN-L (two 120 ohm terminations): add a 120 ohm resistor if neither the unit nor your interface terminates. Swapped CAN-H/CAN-L just gives timeouts; +12 V on a signal pin can destroy the unit.
